Mafia 2 returned to Steam recently, and I missed it on my PS3, plus the removal from Steam, so I thought I'd pick it up.

The gameplay is fairly solid - it's a third person cover shooter, so it's not the hardest thing to grasp. Whilst the shooting is fairly straightforward, the driving is probably most notable aspect of the game, which on the one had is kinda 'sluggish', but on the other hand more 'weighty', so I'm in mixed feelings about it. I have more love for it than hate, though. The story is the real highlight though, which is a brilliant tale of Vito Scaletta, an Italian war veteran becoming increasingly involved with the Mafia familes of Empire Bay a cross between New York and Chicago). In my opinion, the less you know the better, but there's some great twists and turns - all of them plausible - which left me grinning that there are linear shooters that are actually good at what they do.

However, there's a couple of things that I'm not so keen on. The first is the level design - which really mean the map. Whilst I appreciate the open-world 'mimic' of the game, it's essentially one large level, and I'd appreciate if there wasn't so much long distance driving on occasion. The second is the running time, which clocks in at around 12 hours, although it could easily be 10. I'd say I got good value for money considering I paid £4 as it was on sale, the RRP of £20 I can't particularly justify, but it definitely makes a great time sink to kill whilst you're between bigger and more ambitious games. I doubt I'll ever play it again, but I wholeheartedly recommend it.

**6/10: The gameplay stands up, the graphics are nice, but the story is the real shining star here. I thought there could've been more variety in the radio's music, but the game's fairly short length generally balances it out.**
